title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
keyIdea: Keep the k largest numbers seen so far in a min-heap of size k. Its top is the k-th largest. On each add: push, and if the size passes k, pop the smallest.

approaches.name: Sorted array of everything
approaches.idea: Keep all numbers sorted; insert each new one in place; answer all[size − k].
approaches.why: Inserting into a sorted array shifts up to n elements, and the array keeps growing.

approaches.name: Min-heap of size k
approaches.idea: push; if size > k pop; return top.
approaches.why: The heap never holds more than k + 1 numbers.

quiz.q: Why a min-heap and not a max-heap?
options: You need the smallest of the top k: to return it and to drop it when a bigger number arrives

quiz.q: What is the heap's top after each add?
options: The k-th largest number seen so far

quiz.q: Why can a popped number be forgotten forever?
options: k bigger numbers already exist; new numbers can only push it further down
